definitions.explanation: A sweet confection, typically hard candy made from sugar. Different from {雨|あめ} (rain), which has the same pronunciation.

examples.japanese: {飴|あめ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{食|た}べます→食べる：00396_taberu⟧⟦か→か：09473_ka⟧。
examples.english: Do you want to eat some candy?

examples.japanese: ⟦{子|こ}ども→子供：00554_kodomo⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{飴|あめ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦あげました→あげる：00546_ageru⟧。
examples.english: I gave candy to the child.
Candy is good for your throat.

examples.japanese: ⟦ポケット→ポケット：02964_poketto⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{飴|あめ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{入|はい}っていました→入る：00494_hairu⟧。
examples.english: There was candy in my pocket.

examples.japanese: {飴|あめ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{食|た}べ→食べる：00396_taberu⟧⟦ながら→ながら：10530_nagara⟧、⟦{本|ほん}→本：00111_hon⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{読|よ}んでいます→読む：00426_yomu⟧。
examples.english: I'm reading a book while eating candy.

notes:
Primarily refers to hard candy or boiled sweets. Distinguished from ⟦{雨|あめ}→雨：00583_ame⟧ (rain) by kanji, though the pronunciation is the same.

USAGE:
{飴|あめ} traditionally means hard candy made from sugar or starch syrup. In modern usage it can refer to candy more broadly, though ⟦チョコレート→チョコレート：05183_chokoreeto⟧ (chocolate) and ⟦キャンディー→キャンディー：23081_kyandii⟧ (candy, loanword) are used for specific types.

TYPES:
- ⟦のど→喉：00977_nodo⟧{飴|あめ}: throat lozenges
- ⟦{水飴|みずあめ}→水飴：27566_mizuame⟧: starch syrup, liquid candy
- ⟦{金太郎飴|きんたろうあめ}→金太郎飴：30305_kintarouame⟧: patterned candy sticks

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
{飴|あめ}⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{鞭|むち}→鞭：11178_muchi⟧ — literally "candy and whip," equivalent to English "carrot and stick." Describes using rewards and punishments together.

RELATED WORDS:
- ⟦お{菓子|かし}→お菓子：02852_okashi⟧: sweets, snacks (broader category)
- ⟦キャンディー→キャンディー：23081_kyandii⟧: candy (loanword)
